svg.title: EFS blood bank refrigeration controller attack kill chain
svg.desc: Single-lane chain of six stages: refrigeration supervisory controllers exposed to the internet, unconfirmed access through claimed credentials, old firmware or an equipment provider, manipulation of temperature and defrost thresholds on plasma refrigerators at the French Blood Establishment, detection by independent monitoring and alarms before spoilage, the wider European refrigeration attack wave, and response guidance. Detection anchors are management access from non-management networks, setpoint changes without a change ticket and an independent temperature probe.
svg.text: EFS blood bank cold storage: refrigeration controller thresholds raised
Vendor: MDN / NPR / Censys / Claroty (2026-11-06) · Date: 2026-11-07 · Cluster: unattributed · Day 137
REFRIGERATION SUPERVISORY LAYER
Exposure: refrigeration controller web, SSH and Shellinabox reachable from the internet [T1190]
Censys counted 1,825 Danfoss StoreView panels in France on 2026-10-11 (537 by 2026-10-14); Claroty cites thousands exposed
Health-ISAC first advice: remove public internet exposure; CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 says the same (via Censys)
curl -skI https://<controller_ip>/ | grep -i last-modified
Access: unconfirmed - claimed stolen credentials, old firmware, provider channel [T1078 T1133 T1199]
NoName057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance claim European fridge attacks on Telegram; no source ties the claims to EFS
Candidates: Danfoss below 4.2 / R4.3.1, Copeland XWEB Pro up to 1.12.1, equipment-provider remote access (none proven)
xml.cgi action=getauth (CVE-2025-41450 surface)
Manipulation: temperature and defrost thresholds raised on plasma refrigerators [T0836 T0831]
EFS statement 2026-11-03: thresholds raised to extremely high levels overnight on 2026-11-02 at a refrigeration provider
MDN: three cold-storage sites run by Coolworld for EFS; NPR: one vendor, no count; vendor and model not published
setpoint / defrost change without a change ticket
Detection: independent monitoring and alarms caught the deviation [no technique]
EFS monitoring and alarm systems flagged the temperature deviation and staff intervened before the blood spoiled
No temperature values, volumes or detection times published; no product lost per a Keeper Security CISO quoted by MDN
independent probe + out-of-band alarm
Wave context: supermarkets and Estonia [T0886]
French supermarket fridges switched to defrost on 2026-10-11 (Censys); Selver store in Estonia set to +50 C on 2026-11-02
Danfoss says affected units were older models or outdated firmware; Claroty published Danfoss and Copeland flaws 2026-08-09
no CVE shown exploited; none confirmed on CISA KEV in sources read
Response and break points
Health-ISAC bulletin; CISA, FBI, HHS and USDA refrigeration fact sheet 2026-11-05; fixes Danfoss 4.2 / R4.3.1, Copeland 1.13
Segment from enterprise and hospital IT; hard-wired cutoffs and thermal alarms software cannot override; manual control drills
offline backups + physical manual control
Detection anchors
Sigma 01-03, KQL k1-k3, YARA (2 rules), Suricata sids 9950001-9950003, PEAK H1-H3. Low confidence: no IOCs published for the EFS attack.
Break points: no internet exposure, segmentation, firmware fixes, independent probe and alarm, manual control, vendor access review.
